one_month_reasoning: No earnings in the window: Q3 FY27 results are expected in early December 2026 (Q2 was reported Sep 1), and guidance was reaffirmed on Sep 28 [3]. The two big events are already priced: the CEO exit on Sep 28 (stock down about 20-26%) and the Sep 29 investor day (about +7%, new 3-year targets and a $1B buyback) [3][4]. Peer events in the window are the hyperscaler results in late October (AWS/Azure/GCP were very strong last quarter [9]), which would mostly move sentiment. The only other news I can see coming is the CEO search, and a quick permanent appointment (for example Ittycheria staying on) would be mildly positive. After a sharp drop and partial rebound I see no reliable direction, so the ladder is close to symmetric around $356 with about 15% monthly sigma. That is a little below 71%/3.5 = 20%, because realized vol is inflated by the two event days; the $1B buyback gives a slight downside cushion.

fair_value.method: Blend of 40x NTM non-GAAP EPS of about $9.0 at Sep-2027 ($360) and 8x NTM EV/sales on about $3.9B of revenue plus about $3.0B net cash over 85M diluted shares ($403); weighted 50/50, about $380-385.

inputs_detail.input: Long-term revenue growth and margin target
inputs_detail.value: >20% revenue growth; +100-200bp op margin per year; FCF 80-100% of non-GAAP op income

inputs_detail.derivation: $6.49 FY27 mid grown about 22% a year (20% revenue plus about 150bp margin, with share count roughly flat because of the $1B buyback) gives about $7.9 for FY28 and $9.6 for FY29. NTM at Sep-2027 is roughly the average of the two, which I haircut to $9.0 for leadership-transition execution risk.

Today's price is about 55x FY27 and 45x FY28 EPS. Peers growing faster (Snowflake product revenue +37%, Datadog +36%) keep premium multiples, while MDB's total growth is guided to decelerate toward about 20%. A modest de-rating to 40x NTM a year out fits a 20%+ grower with rising margins, and sits inside the $420-470 analyst target range once the lower multiple is applied.

methods.name: EV/sales
methods.inputs: NTM revenue at Sep-2027 ~$3.9B x 8x + net cash ~$3.0B, / 85M shares

inputs_detail.derivation: $3.01B FY27 x 1.20 = $3.61B FY28 and x 1.20 again = $4.33B FY29. NTM at Sep-2027 is about 60/40 FY28/FY29, rounded down to $3.9B.

inputs_detail.value: $2.4B at 2026-07-31, no convert debt shown in recon

inputs_detail.derivation: $2.4B plus about $0.6B FCF a year (Q2 FCF was $137.6M and seasonally rising, with 80-100% conversion targeted). I assume buybacks are roughly offset by the lower share count, so both cash and the share count are held about flat.
85.8M fully diluted weighted shares in Q2, trimmed for the $1B buyback.

Current EV of about $28B is about 8.5x NTM sales. Snowflake and Datadog grow mid-30s and trade richer; Elastic grows 15% and trades far lower. MDB's roughly 20% growth and 76% gross margin put it between them, so I hold about 8x.

bear.story: Atlas growth, stuck at 29% for three quarters, slides toward high-teens. Postgres options inside data platforms (Snowflake Postgres, Databricks Lakebase, DocumentDB with the MongoDB API) and a long CEO search weigh on new-workload wins, and the multiple compresses to about 5x sales.

base.story: Revenue grows about 20% in FY28 as guided and margins expand 100-200bp. AI-native customers (3-5% of Atlas, +165%) add incrementally, a permanent CEO is named, and the multiple de-rates modestly to about 40x NTM EPS.

bull.story: The AI/agent workload wave that is lifting Snowflake, Datadog and the hyperscalers (AWS +37%, GCP +82%) spills into operational databases. Atlas re-accelerates above 30%, Atlas Infinite and Agent Engine gain traction, and the stock regains its $473 high and more.

thesis_break_reason: A price below about $230 (roughly 6x NTM sales, below the 52-week low zone of $216-230) would most likely mean the market sees Atlas growth breaking below about 20% or real share loss to Postgres-based rivals, or a botched CEO succession, rather than ordinary volatility in a 70%-vol name.

reasoning: Company facts: Q2 FY27 revenue $771.8M (+30%), Atlas +29%, non-GAAP operating margin 24%, FCF $137.6M, $2.4B cash; FY27 guided to $2.99-3.03B revenue and $6.39-6.58 EPS [1]. The stock fell after the print because Atlas did not accelerate and Q3 implies about 21% growth [2]. It then fell about 20-26% when CEO Desai left for Meta on Sep 28, with Ittycheria interim and guidance reaffirmed [3], and rebounded about 7% on the Sep 29 investor day, which brought >20% revenue growth and mid-20s Atlas 3-year targets and a $1B buyback [4]. Industry lane: demand across the chain is strong. Hyperscalers accelerated (AWS +37%, Azure +43%, GCP +82%) [9]; Snowflake product revenue +37% with the guide raised [6]; Datadog +36%, and even its non-AI cohort accelerated to the high 20s [7]. Elastic, closer to MDB's developer/search segment, grew only 15%, with annual cloud +27% but monthly self-serve cloud +1% [8]. That points to large-enterprise consumption doing well while small self-serve customers stall, which matches MDB's flat Atlas. Competition is intensifying: Snowflake Postgres and Databricks Lakebase both went GA in Feb 2026 [10][11], and DocumentDB (a Postgres engine with a MongoDB API) is backed by AWS, GCP, Microsoft and Snowflake [12]. Postgres usage is 55.6% of developers against about 26% for MongoDB [13][14]. I see no evidence yet of MDB share loss in reported numbers, so I treat it as a multiple cap rather than a forecast change. Valuation: 40x NTM EPS gives $360 and 8x NTM EV/sales gives $403, for a blended fair value of about $385, roughly 8% above the $356 spot; analyst targets sit higher at $420-470 [5]. Scenarios: bear $220 (25%), base $380 (50%), bull $540 (25%), a mean of about $380. For the ladder I used a lognormal-like distribution with a median of about $356-365 and sigma of about 0.5 (below the 71% realized vol, which is inflated by the event days), with a slightly fat right tail to reflect AI optionality. Research was limited: SEC rate limits blocked the investor-day 8-K, and DB-Engines was unreachable.
